source_grounding.call_chain_traced: euclid_similarity (simple.rs:214, internal score = -Sigma((a-b)^2); trait doc 'Greater the value - closer the vectors') -> Distance::postprocess_score (types.rs:320, Euclid -> EuclidMetric::postprocess) -> postprocess = score.abs().sqrt() (simple.rs:74-78, trait doc 'correct metric score for displaying') -> local_shard/search.rs:156-158 applies it on QueryEnum::Nearest with the comment 'Don't post-process if we are dealing with custom scoring' -> API ScoredPoint.score documented as 'Points vector distance to the query vector' (types.rs:380-381) and Distance::Euclid = Order::SmallBetter (types.rs:347). Net displayed score for an Euclid nearest query = raw Euclidean distance d: self-match d=0 -> score 0.0, and the observed 1.7320508 / 2.236068 are exactly sqrt(3) / sqrt(5), the seeded distances of ids 104/109 from the query vector [0,0,0,0]. The legacy 1/(1+d) convention the script assumed exists nowhere in the v1.18.0 tree (whole-tree grep for '1.0 / (1.0 +' hits only unrelated turboquant erf approximations).
source_grounding.by_design_evidence_note: Explicit intent evidence per the v3.4 tightened rule: (a) docstring on MetricPostProcessing 'correct metric score for displaying' + Euclid impl score.abs().sqrt() — the displayed score is intentionally the processed (raw-distance) value; (b) field docstring 'Points vector distance to the query vector' on ScoredPoint.score — the API score is declared to BE the distance; (c) inline comment 'Don't post-process if we are dealing with custom scoring' — deliberate per-variant handling; (d) Distance::Euclid -> Order::SmallBetter — smaller-score-is-better is coherent only with a distance-valued score. This is not bare unannotated behavior.
